haiku-low.q1: Reports of 10,000 rows or fewer stream the CSV directly as the click's response. Larger ones (above 10,000) queue a background job, and the user later gets an emailed download link.
haiku-low.q2: The API returns the existing queued or running export record. A unique rule stops a second export from starting, so no new job is created.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 24 hours. The bucket's existing 7-day rule deletes the stored file. There is no cleanup job, and the export record stays.
haiku-low.q4: Three attempts, retried after 60 and 300 seconds. After the last failure, the state becomes failed and the user is emailed report_export_failed, though that email may not be sent.
haiku-low.q5: Both paths read report rows from the read replica. The export record lives in the primary database, but report rows are never read from the primary.
haiku-low.q6: Status is stored in the report_exports table in the primary database. The page polls GET /exports/latest every 5 seconds while queued or running, and on reopen it fetches the latest state.
haiku-low.q7: It reads rows in row_id order, a few thousand per query, and writes CSV into one roughly 8 MB multipart upload part at a time, so the full file is never held in memory.
haiku-low.q8: A failed attempt aborts the upload, so nothing becomes visible. The next attempt restarts from the beginning and rewrites the same file name. A dead worker's open upload is discarded by the bucket after 24 hours.
haiku-low.q9: The filters and column order are stored in the report_exports record. The job receives only the export id as payload and loads the filters and columns from that record.
haiku-low.q10: A unique rule on the report_exports table, covering user and report for queued or running states, enforces it. The document does not say more about the mechanism.
haiku-low.q11: The file's upload must complete before the email is sent. If the job runs again after the export is done, it sees done and stops. If the file is not finished, it rebuilds and replaces the file.
haiku-low.q12: The response breaks off and the browser shows a failed download. No record, job or stored file is created, and the user can click again.

sonnet.q1: Row count decides: reports.row_count of 10,000 or fewer is small; above 10,000 is large (unfiltered count, so filtered exports of large reports still go large). Small: the response to the click is the CSV, sent as a file download, nothing stored. Large: a background job builds the file, which is saved in the exports bucket and linked by email; the click returns the export record straight away and the page shows its state.
sonnet.q2: The unique rule allows only one record per user and report in state queued or running, so the insert finds the existing one; the API returns that existing record and stops. No second export or job is started.
sonnet.q3: The link works for 24 hours (the storage maximum). The file is removed by the bucket's existing 7-day rule; there is no cleanup job.
sonnet.q4: At most 3 attempts (retries after 60 s, then 300 s). After attempt 3 fails, the final-failure handler sets the state to failed (the page shows failed and the user can start a new export) and sends the report_export_failed email, though that email might not arrive if the handler fails.
sonnet.q5: The read replica, never the primary (both the small path and the job). Only the report_exports table lives in the primary.
sonnet.q6: In the export record (report_exports table) in the primary database. The page calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest on load and polls it every 5 seconds while the state is queued or running; reopening later just loads and fetches the newest record's state. No download link is shown on the page.
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads rows from the replica in row_id order, a few thousand per query, writes CSV into a multipart upload, keeping only one part (about 8 MB) in memory at a time and uploading it when full. So the ~900 MB file fits in 512 MB. Whether it finishes within 30 minutes is unmeasured.
sonnet.q8: The job aborts the upload and raises, and an aborted upload leaves nothing behind; nothing is visible until the upload completes. If the worker dies or times out, the upload can't be aborted and the bucket discards it after 24 hours. The next attempt starts from the beginning, writing to the same fixed file name; state stays running between attempts.
sonnet.q9: They are stored in the export record in the report_exports table (primary database). The job's payload is only the export id; the job loads the record to get them.
sonnet.q10: The unique rule (constraint) on the report_exports table for user and report in state queued or running; the insert enforces it, and the API returns the existing record.
sonnet.q11: The file must be built and the multipart upload completed (step 3 succeeded), then a 24-hour download link is created and emailed, and only afterwards is the state set to done. On a repeat run: if the record is already done, the job stops. If the first run hasn't finished, both write the same file name and the last completed upload wins. If the email call raises, the whole job retries, rebuilding and replacing the file; a rare repeat email is accepted.
sonnet.q12: The response breaks off and the browser shows a failed download. Nothing was stored (no record, no job, no file). The user can click again.
